_description: Task13 DRIFT field, FINE transcription -- the 0.1mm grid used for BOTH the near-field solve and the final stitched volume. The coarse sibling (example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_task13_coarse.json) is the 0.4mm far-field grid. PAD/GAP SPLIT: this file uses pixelSize 3.5 / pixelGap 0.9 while the coarse file uses 3.6 / 0.8. That is NOT a typo -- both are the same 4.4mm pitch, and each file uses the split that divides its OWN spacing exactly: 3.5/0.1=35 and 0.9/0.1=9 here, versus 3.6/0.4=9 and 0.8/0.4=2 there. This file's split cannot be used at the coarse spacing (3.5/0.4=8.75), which is the whole reason there are two files. CATHODE FORMULA, so the value can be recomputed by hand when the drift length or the bulk field changes: CathodePotential = -BulkField * (driftZDepth - pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition). The drift length is 69.9 - 10.0 = 59.9mm, so 50 V/mm gives -50 * 59.9 = -2995 V. This file holds -3000, i.e. 50.08 V/mm nominal. The value is maintained BY HAND on purpose, so the bulk field stays a visible, editable number rather than a derived one. TILE SIZE: Npixels 5, i.e. a 5x5 pad tile at the 4.4mm pitch. GridPotential does NOT enter this calculation: the shield grid has holes and is transparent at the tile centre, so it is not an equipotential plane terminating the field -- on the earlier 149.9mm/-7500 V run, measured phi at the grid plane z=11.6mm was about -71 V, nothing like GridPotential. The bulk field is set by the CATHODE against the PIXEL PLANE at 0 V. GridPotential instead sets the collection field between the grid and the pads.
